entries.test: Published research on whether training on large amounts of model-generated content degrades or improves model performance.
entries.note: Later work shows curated synthetic data is widely used to good effect. That cuts against the broad claim, but uncurated recursive training does show collapse.

entries.test: Disclosures of training data, or evidence from litigation, showing whether OpenAI's training corpora (e.g. Common Crawl) included Axel Springer publications such as Business Insider or Politico.
entries.note: 'I'd bet money' expresses firm confidence, not a stated probability. The full training data is not public, but the contents of Common Crawl are.
This is a strategic recommendation to OpenAI.

entries.test: Whether later OpenAI image and video models reduced visual errors, and whether that came mainly from more training data or from other methods.
entries.note: OpenAI does not fully disclose what drove the gains, so attribution may be contested.

entries.test: Whether labs hit a binding shortage of training data, and whether synthetic data failed to address it, according to lab disclosures and analyses such as Epoch AI's.
entries.note: It is part of his rebuttal to the argument for small synthetic-data models.
'Likely because' hedges his explanation of why the article is vague.

entries.test: Reported or disclosed terms of Anthropic's cloud spending commitments to Google Cloud and AWS.
entries.note: It rests on an unnamed source.
'Isn't exactly exciting' is a judgment of worth. Microsoft actually said 6 percentage points of growth, which he reads as 6% of the growth.

entries.test: Whether global equity indices had their best first quarter in five years in Q1 2024, and whether commentators attributed this to the AI boom.
entries.note: Only the market fact is checkable. The 'I fear' hype-cycle part is hedged and evaluative.

entries.test: As of early 2024: the major cloud providers' data center spending and their own statements on AI revenue, compared with the profits of AI integrators and sellers versus infrastructure suppliers.
entries.note: 'Yet to prove its necessity' is an evaluative aside.

entries.test: Enterprise AI adoption surveys from early 2024, such as Census Bureau BTOS figures and McKinsey's survey.
entries.note: He phrases it as his own perception, but the plain reading is that AI adoption was low.

entries.test: Whether hallucination rates were reduced by methods other than more compute and data, such as retrieval or post-training, according to benchmarks like Vectara's hallucination leaderboard.
entries.note: The 'only way' wording makes this a strong exclusivity claim.

entries.test: Whether major 2023 and early 2024 press coverage of OpenAI's and Anthropic's revenues discussed their profitability or losses.
entries.note: In April 2024 Anthropic's revenue was not yet multi-billion.

entries.test: Whether Sora and similar video models failed to launch or gain meaningful adoption, or were abandoned, after release.
entries.note: 'Dead on arrival' is hyperbolic, but its plain reading is commercial failure.

entries.test: Whether a market turn against AI, following a failure to adopt it at scale, leads to cutbacks of tens of thousands of jobs.
entries.note: It has no deadline and depends on both a lack of adoption and a market turn.

entries.test: Whether Nvidia's orders and data center revenue slow dramatically after AI fails to produce meaningful profits for customers and providers.
entries.note: The canary part is hedged with 'likely'. Only the firm conditional is graded.

entries.test: Whether, after a fall in Nvidia, the major cloud providers suffer larger losses in stock value or financial results tied to their AI spending.
entries.note: 'I expect' is firm expectation. The drafter's 'likely' modality understates it.
Readers would judge 'physics getting in the way of progressing much further' in different ways. 'Mediocre' is a value judgment.
